 - AFFECTED PAGE -> PAGE ID. DriftReport.Pages carries the wiki-relative PATH only, deliberately: the planner is pure over (changed files, tree pages) and knows nothing about state. So `--mark` joins DriftReport.Pages by path onto state.Pages to get pageId, and a page with no pageId (never published) has no label to add — REPORT it and skip, do not fail the run. That join is the reason state stays out of the planner: the writer owns it.
 - THE LABEL WRITE. ConfluenceClient.AddLabelsAsync is built and WireMock-tested from M2 (M2 slice 3). Adding a label a page already carries is idempotent in Confluence, but check the state flag first and skip pages already `stale: true` so a re-run costs zero requests — same discipline as dashboard's skip-if-unchanged.

WHAT SLICE 1 SETTLED — DO NOT RE-DERIVE (commit 51e5f49, 809 tests, was 784):
 - THE GLOB MATCHER IS Microsoft.Extensions.FileSystemGlobbing's Matcher, Ordinal, one per distinct pattern. Do not add a second globbing dependency and do not hand-roll `**`.
 - TWO PATTERN SPELLINGS ARE NORMALIZED BEFORE MATCHING and nothing else is: a trailing slash (`src/Rates/` -> `src/Rates/**`) and a gitignore-style leading slash (`/src/**` -> `src/**`). Matcher matches NO file for either as written, forever, and a glob that can never fire is the failure mode of an advisory check that gets believed — nobody investigates a green run. A pattern with no wildcard still names exactly one file, per glob semantics, because guessing otherwise would make `sources` mean something different from `wiki.exclude`. Both normalizations are pinned by tests and fired live.
 - `sources` GLOBS AND THE DIFF ARE BOTH RELATIVE TO THE docume.json DIRECTORY. The git call is `git -C <configDir> diff --name-only --relative --no-renames baseline..head -- .`, which is also why a changed file outside that directory can never match. GitRepository now has ONE private DiffAsync behind both public methods.
 - A BAD BASELINE THROWS, LOUD, WITH THE SHA NAMED (GitException -> exit 1 on stderr). Zero drift is what a green advisory check shows, so a zero that really means "git could not resolve the baseline" (shallow CI clone, force-pushed branch) is the one wrong answer here that gets believed. Same reason no baseline at all fails instead of defaulting to something arbitrary.
 - THE REPORT CARRIES BOTH DENOMINATORS AND A SourcesUndeclared FLAG, and the three verdicts are distinct in every format: "no documented sources touched" vs "no page declares a sources: glob, so drift can never be reported" vs N affected. The second one is a switched-off feature and must never read as a clean bill of health.
 - EXIT CODE 0 EVEN ON DRIFT unless --fail-on-drift (§6.4: advisory). A failed RUN is always 1, and in the machine formats always on stderr — including an invalid --format value, because a CI step piping stdout into a PR comment must not post the error as the comment.
 - THE COMMENT'S MARKER IS `<!-- docume:drift -->` (DriftComment.Marker), first line, so a CI job edits its own comment instead of piling up. The renderer is pure and clock-free for the same reason DashboardPage is.

DECISION FOR .claude/references/decisions.md (PENDING — the headless loop cannot write .claude/): ## 2026-07-24 — HTML entities: publish the resolved character, not the entity name A named or numeric character reference is published as the character it resolves to (Markdig's HtmlEntityInline.Transcoded), written back through WriteEscaped, rather than echoed as the source spelling. WHY: storage format is XML, and XML predefines only five entity names (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos). An HTML-only name such as © or   is UNDEFINED in an XML document, so echoing it invites Confluence to reject the body or silently rewrite it on save. A server-side rewrite is §8 content-hash drift, which invalidates an approval when nothing really changed (§9.2). Resolved characters are plain UTF-8 and unambiguous. This is the same reasoning as the strikethrough decision, which emits the editor's own rather than the shape that reads best in source. CONSEQUENCE: re-escaping keeps the round-trip honest. & transcodes to '&' and is written back as '&', never '&'. &/</> come out byte-identical; "/' resolve to a bare " and ', which need no escaping in element content and are re-escaped by WriteAttributeEscaped when the text lands in an attribute instead. CONSEQUENCE TO WATCH IN THE SANDBOX: page bodies now contain non-ASCII characters (©, —, →, …, U+00A0, astral codepoints). Confirm Confluence round-trips them byte-identically on save rather than re-encoding them as numeric character references. U+00A0 is the likeliest to be normalized by the editor. A re-encode would be §8 hash drift on any page containing a symbol. NOT DECIDED HERE: an unrecognized reference. Markdig never makes a node for '&nosuchthing;' or '©' with no semicolon — it leaves a LiteralInline, which already published correctly escaped, so no code was needed and none was written. move-reorder-api.settledFrom: Atlassian's own REST docs (v1 api-group-content---children-and-descendants), the 2020-03-27 developer-community announcement, and Atlassian support's move/copy page doc. No live call — no sandbox space exists yet.

answers.a-exists-on-cloud: YES. Documented under v1 "Content — children and descendants", shipped 2020-03-27, NOT marked deprecated or experimental. Scopes: write:confluence-content (classic) / write:page:confluence (granular) — the same scope the publish already uses. 200 answers {"pageId": "<id>"}; documented errors are 400, 403, 404. v2 has NO move verb at all, so this is the only endpoint for it.
answers.b-does-it-spend-a-page-version: NO (docs + structure; not live-verified). The endpoint takes NO request body and therefore no version number, so unlike every other write it sits outside Confluence's optimistic-lock contract — there is no version to send and none comes back. Atlassian's support doc for move states a moved page keeps its full page history. THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERED: a reorder/move cannot silently revoke approval. Belt-and-braces anyway, because DocuMe keys invalidation off contentHash, which is body-only (§9.2) — even a version bump could not revoke approval here. DEFENSIVE DESIGN ADOPTED: never assume a moved page's version; the update path already re-reads remote version before every write (PublishExecutor.cs:312), so a stale Version in state costs nothing. Confirm on the first sandbox run.
answers.c-can-append-reparent: YES, and it is the cheaper move. `append` = "move the page to be a child of the target", so one bodyless PUT reparents. The v2 alternative (PUT /pages/{id} with a new parentId) works — DocuMe already sends parentId there, ConfluenceRequests.cs:36 — but requires the body and version.number, spending a page version for a change that touched no content. Use v1 move for a parent-only change; keep the v2 parentId for the case where the body is being rewritten anyway.
answers.d-stale-or-missing-target: 404, and it does NOT discriminate: page-gone and target-gone arrive identically. Handled by naming both ids in the operation string so the caller can tell a re-plan (target moved) from a recreate (page vanished). 403 is a permission refusal (moving needs edit on both pages) and stops the run per rule §1.2.

move-reorder-api.designImpact: One verb covers BOTH remaining M2 items: `append` is the §6.2 page move, `before`/`after` are the child-page ordering post-pass PLAN.md §6.2 line 246 asks for ("reconcile each parent's child order ... using minimal move operations; disable with --no-reorder"). Atlassian's own caution is load-bearing and is documented on ConfluencePageMovePosition: NEVER use before/after when the target is a top-level page — it moves the page to the space top level where it does not appear in the page tree. DocuMe's tree always hangs under confluence.rootPageId (§5.1), so a reorder reorders children of a known parent; the client cannot enforce this (it would need a read) so the caller owns it.
